title: Recounting the Journey

questions.question: Where did Moses speak these words to Israel?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 1:1, 5 (ESV): "These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel beyond the Jordan in the wilderness... On this side of the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses undertook to explain this law..."

questions.question: How long should the journey from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea have taken?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 1:2 (ESV): "It is eleven days’ journey from Horeb by the way of Mount Seir to Kadesh-barnea."

questions.question: Why did Moses appoint leaders over the people?
options: To judge disputes because he couldn’t bear it alone
questions.correctAnswer: To judge disputes because he couldn’t bear it alone
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 1:9, 12 (ESV): "At that time I said to you, ‘I am not able to bear you by myself... How can I bear by myself the weight and burden of you and your strife?’"

questions.question: What did the spies report about the land God gave them?
options: It was good but had strong inhabitants
questions.correctAnswer: It was good but had strong inhabitants
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 1:25 (ESV): "And they took in their hands some of the fruit of the land and brought it down to us, and brought us word again and said, ‘It is a good land that the LORD our God is giving us.’" (Context of vv. 27–28 shows fear of strong people.)

questions.question: What was God’s punishment for Israel’s rebellion at Kadesh-barnea?
options: None of that generation would enter the land except Caleb and Joshua
questions.correctAnswer: None of that generation would enter the land except Caleb and Joshua
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 1:35–36 (ESV): "‘Not one of these men of this evil generation shall see the good land... except Caleb... and Joshua..."

questions.question: What qualification did the appointed leaders need?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 1:13 (ESV): "Choose for your tribes wise, understanding, and experienced men, and I will appoint them as your heads."

questions.question: How many people did Moses say Israel had become?
options: As the sand of the sea
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 1:10 (ESV): "The Lord your God has multiplied you, and behold, you are today as numerous as the stars of heaven."

questions.question: What command did Moses give the judges regarding judgment?
options: Do not be partial in judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Do not be partial in judgment
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 1:17 (ESV): "You shall not be partial in judgment. You shall hear the small and the great alike."

questions.question: Why were they told not to be intimidated by anyone?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 1:17 (ESV): "You shall not be intimidated in judgment, for the judgment is God's."

questions.question: Where did the spies go up to?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 1:24 (ESV): "And they turned and went up into the hill country, and came to the Valley of Eshcol and spied it out."

questions.question: What metaphor did Moses use for how God carried them?
options: As an eagle carries its young
As a man carries his son
As a shepherd carries a sheep
questions.correctAnswer: As a man carries his son
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 1:31 (ESV): "And in the wilderness, where you have seen how the Lord your God carried you, as a man carries his son..."

questions.question: Who specifically was promised to enter the land and encourage the people?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 1:38 (ESV): "Joshua the son of Nun, who stands before you, he shall enter. Encourage him, for he shall cause Israel to inherit it."

questions.question: What happened when the people tried to fight the Amorites after God said not to?
options: The Amorites chased them like bees
questions.correctAnswer: The Amorites chased them like bees
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 1:44 (ESV): "Then the Amorites... came out against you and chased you as bees do and beat you down..."

questions.question: Where did the people stay for "many days" after this defeat?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 1:46 (ESV): "So you remained at Kadesh many days, the days that you remained there."

questions.question: What reason did the people give for not wanting to go up (murmuring in their tents)?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 1:27 (ESV): "And you murmured in your tents and said, 'Because the Lord hates us he has brought us out of the land of Egypt...'"

key_verse_text: and in the wilderness, where you have seen how the LORD your God carried you, as a man carries his son, all the way that you went until you came to this place. (ESV)
